system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented great-power competition amid tech, energy, and financial shocks
system_description.narrative_summary: The international order is an open, tightly coupled system driven by intensifying great‑power rivalry, rapid diffusion of strategic technologies (notably AI), and multiple concurrent regional conflicts that stress energy and maritime chokepoints. Those pressures are transmitted quickly into global finance and markets—bond volatility, commodity shocks and capital flows—while domestic political volatility and elections amplify feedbacks and contingency. The system is therefore more brittle and reactive: small shocks (attacks on ships, AI safety incidents, election surprises) cascade across security, energy, and financial subsystems.
system_description.scope: Nation‑states and their alliances; regional conflict theatres and non‑state armed actors; global energy and maritime flows (oil, diesel, tankers, Strait of Hormuz); international financial markets and capital flows (bonds, equities, reserves); major technology firms, AI models, and governance/regulatory responses; international institutions and emergency stockpile mechanisms.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio‑technical and economic system—globalized human civilization integrating security, political economy, technology, and ecological constraints.
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy & maritime logistics (oil production, shipping routes, strategic chokepoints)
Global financial and capital markets (sovereign yields, bond markets, cross‑border capital flows)
Advanced technology & AI ecosystem (chip supply chains, models, corporate governance, national policy)
Regional security theatres and conflict networks (Ukraine, Middle East/Iran‑Houthis, Horn of Africa, North Korea)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed by varying NATO/EU support, are locked in a prolonged high-intensity conflict as Moscow intensifies strikes and Kyiv seeks advanced weapons, funding and diplomatic backing.

variables.name: Middle East maritime and energy security
variables.description: Iran, Houthi forces, Saudi Arabia and regional actors are escalating attacks on shipping and oil infrastructure, disrupting Red Sea and Hormuz routes and straining global fuel flows and logistics.

variables.name: US–China strategic competition
variables.description: The United States and China are deepening strategic rivalry across trade, technology, investment and diplomatic arenas as measures to contain, decouple and contest influence accelerate.

variables.name: AI governance and industrial power shift
variables.description: Major tech companies, investors and national regulators are racing to shape AI deployment, safety regimes and markets as rapid model rollouts and compute concentration reallocate economic and geopolitical leverage.

variables.name: North Korea missile–nuclear escalation
variables.description: North Korea is expanding and flight-testing intermediate- and long-range missile capabilities while issuing threats to neighbours, raising the risk of regional nuclear flashpoints and allied military responses.
